title: WPMS/2548/2021 of RAJENDRA KUMAR KALRA Vs UNION OF INDIA

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 2548 of 2021
Rajendra Kumar Kalra and another .....Petitioners.
Versus
Union of India and others .... Respondents
Present :
Mr. S. Bhupendra Singh, Advocate, for the petitioner.
Mr. V.K. Kaparuwan, Standing Counsel for Union of India / respondents.
JUDGEMENT
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
The respondents by proceeding, to take an action
under Section 164 (2) of the Companies Act, 2013, has
disqualified the petitioners from the Directorship for a period
from 30th November, 2018 to 29th November, 2023, as a
consequence of which, the petitioners had been rendered
incapacitated to utilise their Din Nos. 01960384 and
02046080 respectively.
2. The petitioners had come up with the case, that if
the provisions contained under Section 164 of the Companies
Act, is taken into consideration, if a person is to be held to be
ineligible to be appointed as a Director of the Company, the
procedure for his disqualification has had to be resorted to as
per stipulations and procedure contained under Section 164
to be read with Section 167, as provided under the
Companies Act.
3. The learned counsel for the petitioners had in para
13 as well as in para 14 of the Writ Petition, has specifically

2
come up with the case, that the impugned notices of
disqualifying the petitioners to function as Director, which
was issued while exercising the powers under Section 164 of
the Act, happens to be in violation of the principles of natural
justice, as prior to passing of the orders of disqualifying the
petitioners to function as Director of the Company, no
opportunity of hearing was ever provided and even that is not
reflected from the order impugned, which is under challenge,
where disqualification has been imposed upon the petitioners
for a period w.e.f. 30th November, 2018 to 29th November,
2023.
4. The learned counsel for the petitioners has
confined his argument from the perspective, that since
disqualifying the petitioner to function as a Director, under
Section 164 (2) of the Act, it has a civil consequences, in that
eventuality, the Director, against whom, the action has been
proposed to be taken for disqualifying him to function as a
Director of the Company, while exercising powers under
Section 164 of the Act, he ought to have been heard before
taking of any actual action.
5. In support of his contention, the learned counsel
for the petitioners has referred to a judgement rendered by
the Division Bench of the Allahabad High Court on 16th
January, 2020, in a bunch of Writ Petitions, with the leading
Writ Petition No. 12498 of 2019, Jai Shankar Agrahari
Vs. Union of India and another.
6. The issue involved therein, in the bunch of Writ

3
Petitions, as it was decided by the Allahabad High Court
could be summarised in view of the observations, which has
been made in para-1 of the judgement, which is extracted
hereunder :-
"1. In all these writ petitions, petitioners were
Directors of various Companies and have been declared
disqualified to continue as Directors of all the
Companies in which they were Directors, under Section
164 (2) of Companies Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred to
as "Act, 2013"), for a period of five years. Petitioners,
therefore, have challenged declaration made by
Registrar of Companies, U. P, Kanpur (hereinafter
referred to as "ROC") publishing notice of such
disqualification of petitioners specifying the period of
five years and in most cases it is from 01.11.2016 to
31.10.2021 while in some cases period of five years
varies but total period of disqualification is five years.
Petitioners have prayed for quashing of aforesaid
declaration made by ROC. They have also sought a
mandamus directing respondents to reactivate
petitioners' Director Identification Number (hereinafter
referred to as 'DIN') and restore their names on the Roll
of Directors."
7. In that case too, the petitioners therein were
disqualified to continue as Director of the Company and there
too the order was passed by the Registrar of the Company,
while exercising its power under Section 164 (2) of the Act
of 2013, for a period of five years.
8. The said matter was quite elaborately considered
by the Division Bench of Allahabad High Court, and while
concluding its finding, the Division Bench in its para 84 has
observed, that since apparently, the action taken by the
Registrar of Companies, while exercising powers under
Section 164 (2) of the Act of disqualifying the Director to

4
function and cancelling their DIN number, it was in violation
of the Rule 11 of the Rules framed under the Act, as no
opportunity of hearing was provided. The Division Bench of
Allahabad High Court had made reference to the ratio
propounded by the Gujrat High Court, as well as the
judgment of the Division Bench of the Lucknow Bench of
Allahabad High Court, as rendered in Mohd. Tariq
Siddiqui, and accordingly, the bunch of Writ Petitions were
disposed of by the observation which were made in 84, which
is extracted hereunder :-
"84. ROC, now, shall be at liberty to give a notice
to petitioners to verify and establish the facts whether
disqualification alleges to have been suffered by
petitioners-Directors so as to attract Section 164 (2) of
Act, 2013, actually exist or not. After giving them
opportunity and being satisfied that such
disqualification has occurred, it will proceed further in
accordance with law."
9. This judgement of the Division Bench dated 16th
January, 2020, it had left open for the Register of the
Company, that if at all, it contemplates to take any action of
disqualifying the petitioners therein, to function as a Director
of the Company or was creating any restriction in utilisation
of DIN number, it was left open for the respondents, to give
an opportunity of hearing and then only to proceed to pass an
order under Section 164 (2) of the Act.
10. This Division Bench judgement of 16th January,
2020, was subsequently followed by yet another Division
Bench of Allahabad High Court in Writ Petition No. 25199

5
of 2020, Vinod Kumar Gupta Vs. Union of India and
others, as decided on 27th January, 2021.
11. Owing to the fact that the aforesaid judgements of
Allahabad High Court, it had rather only confined its
interpretation from the limited scope of exercise of powers
under Section 164 (2) of the Act, that if at all, there was any
disqualification, which was to be rendered against the
Director of the Company under the provisions of the
Companies Act, in that eventuality, the order of
disqualification could only be resorted to, after issuing a prior
notice and providing an opportunity of hearing.
12. Apparently, as per Annexure Nos. 1 and 2 to the
present Writ Petition, where the petitioners had been
disqualified for a period referred therein to function as
Director for five years, it does not spell out, that ever the
petitioners were given a prior notice or the petitioners were
heard, and it also do not disclose the reasoning for passing
the order.
13. Hence, owning to the principles of the Division
Bench of Allahabad High Court, which stood affirmed by the
subsequent Division Bench also, this Writ Petition too would
stand disposed of in the light of observation made in para 84
of the Division Bench judgement as rendered on 16th January,
2020. It will be open for the respondent No. 2, that if at all,
any action is required to be taken under Section 164 (2) of
the Act, that could only be taken after providing an
opportunity of hearing to the petitioners.

6
14. Owing to the aforesaid directions given by the
Division Bench, which is factually a pre-condition which is
not objected by the respondents Counsel, this Writ Petition
too would stand decided in terms of para 84 of the judgment
of Division Bench of Allahabad High Court dated 16th
January, 2020, and the impugned notices, Annexure No.1 and
2, would stand quashed, subject to the liberty reserved for the
respondent No. 2, as provided in para 84 of the Division
Bench judgment of Allahabad High Court dated 16th January,
2020, to proceed in accordance with Section 164 (2) of the
Companies Act, for the purposes of declaring or
disqualifying the petitioners as Director under Section 167
(1) of the Companies Act. It will be open for the respondents
to proceed so, as per the directions given by the Division
Bench.
15. Subject to the aforesaid, the Writ Petition stands
disposed of.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 13.06.2022
Shiv
